lead: A dynamometer is a brake that measures the torque it absorbs. The engine turns, the dynamometer resists, and a torque arm and load cell turn that resistance into a number. A test cell is the room built around that brake: rigid bed, guarded coupling, fuel and coolant lines, exhaust extraction, fire safety and a panel that logs speed, torque, temperatures and flows. Together they make an engine measurement repeatable and safe. Every brake power figure in 5.1 and 5.2 comes from a dynamometer.
prereq: You need: brake power from torque and speed in 5.2, and bmep in 5.1.

blocks.text: A dynamometer must do two things: absorb the engine's power as heat or electricity, and measure the reaction torque on its casing. The simplest absorption brake is the Prony brake. A wooden block presses on the flywheel, a lever arm of length L carries a spring balance, and the friction force at the rim is read as a weight. For a rope brake, a rope passes over the flywheel and two balances read the tight and slack sides.

Torque is force times perpendicular distance: T = W × L, where T is torque in N·m, W is the net force on the arm in N and L is the arm length in m. If the balance has a dead weight S with no load, use W = (reading − S). Brake power follows from torque and speed.

blocks.where: BP is brake power in W; N is engine speed in rev/min; T is torque in N·m. For a torque arm, T = W × L, with W in N and L in m.

items: Prony and rope brakes: cheap, no external power, but friction fades with heat, poor at high speed, needs water cooling and a long arm.
Hydraulic (water) brake: rotor and stator with water between; load set by water quantity; torque arm measures reaction; good for high power.
Eddy-current brake: electromagnet drags a steel disc; load set by coil current; heat removed by water jacket; fast control.

DC machine: as a generator it absorbs power into a resistor bank (this is the absorption use); the same machine can also motor, driving the engine without fuel; heavier and slower than an eddy-current brake.

blocks.text: An absorption brake can only load the engine. A motoring dynamometer is an electric machine that can also drive the engine. A DC machine motoring at controlled speed gives the motoring test: the engine is turned without fuel, and the shaft power needed equals friction power (5.2). The same machine can generate, so one unit covers both directions.

A transient dynamometer goes further. It changes speed and torque fast enough to follow a driving cycle second by second. An AC dynamometer uses a vector-controlled induction or synchronous machine with low inertia. It works in four quadrants: forward motoring, forward generating, reverse motoring, reverse generating. That lets it reproduce a stop-start city pattern, a cold start, or a turbo lag event.

An absorption dynamometer cannot do this. It cannot motor the engine, and it cannot hold a prescribed speed-torque trace second by second, even though an eddy-current unit changes load faster than a water brake. It only holds a steady speed while the operator sets load.

sections.h3: The test cell makes the measurement repeatable

blocks.text: A test cell is a room designed around the dynamometer. The engine sits on a rigid bed, often on anti-vibration mounts, aligned to the dynamometer shaft. The coupling between engine and dynamometer carries a fixed guard: a spinning shaft at 5000 rev/min must never be exposed.

Services are fixed: fuel supply with a measured tank or flow meter (5.3), coolant circuit with a heat exchanger and temperature control, ventilation to supply combustion air and remove fumes, exhaust extraction to carry gases outside, and fire detection with a clean-agent extinguisher.
The instrument panel logs speed, torque, temperatures and flows at the same time. Repeatability comes from keeping all of these the same from run to run.

items: Warm the engine to a steady coolant temperature.
Set the speed and load on the dynamometer controller.
Log torque, speed, fuel flow and temperatures together.
Repeat the point once to check drift.

figure.caption: The tree splits dynamometers into absorption machines that only load the engine and motoring machines that can also drive it. The motoring branch is what makes a driving cycle possible.

examples.question: A hydraulic dynamometer has a torque arm of 0.5 m. At 1500 rev/min the spring balance reads 120 N. The engine is a 1.0 L four-stroke. Find the torque, the brake power and the bmep.
steps: Torque: T = W × L = 120 N × 0.5 m = 60 N·m.
Brake power: with T = 60 N·m, BP = 2πNT/60 = (2π × 1500 × 60 N·m) / 60 = 9425 W = 9.42 kW.
bmep: bmep = 2π n<sub>R</sub> T / V<sub>d</sub> = 2π × 2 × 60 / (1.0 × 10<sup>-3</sup>) = 7.54 × 10<sup>5</sup> Pa = 7.54 bar.
examples.answer: T = 60 N·m, BP = 9.42 kW, bmep = 7.54 bar.
examples.check:
import math
W = 120.0
L = 0.5
N = 1500.0
Vd = 1.0e-3
nR = 2
T = W * L
BP = 2 * math.pi * N * T / 60
bmep = 2 * math.pi * nR * T / Vd
print(round(T, 2))
print(round(BP / 1000, 2))
print(round(bmep / 1e5, 2))

traps: Using the arm diameter instead of the radius. The torque arm length L is measured from the shaft centre to the balance.
Forgetting the dead weight. A balance that reads S with no load gives net force W = reading − S.
Forgetting the 60 when N is in rev/min. With N in rev/min, BP = 2πNT/60; the 60 converts minutes to seconds. With ω in rad/s, use BP = Tω.
Mixing mm and m. A 500 mm arm is 0.5 m, not 500.
Confusing bmep with brake power. bmep is pressure, in bar or Pa; BP is power, in kW.

quiz.q: What does a dynamometer measure directly: torque, power or speed?
quiz.a: Torque. Power is computed from torque and speed.

quiz.q: Why does a Prony brake lose accuracy at high speed?
quiz.a: Friction heat fades the lining, the block or rope loses grip, water cooling becomes uneven, and the arm vibrates.

quiz.q: A torque arm of 0.4 m carries 80 N at 2000 rev/min. Find T and BP.
Why can an absorption dynamometer not follow a city driving cycle?
quiz.a: It cannot drive the engine and it cannot change speed fast. It only holds a steady load set by the operator or a slow controller.

quiz.q: A rope brake has a dead weight of 10 N. At 1800 rev/min the balance reads 90 N; the effective radius of the rope on the flywheel is 0.5 m. Find T and BP.
State one difference between a motoring dynamometer and a generator dynamometer.
quiz.a: A motoring dynamometer is built to drive the engine at controlled speed; a plain generator dynamometer is used only to absorb and measure power. A DC machine can do both, but the two functions are separate tests.

quiz.q: Why is the coupling guard a safety requirement, not an option?
quiz.a: The shaft spins at high speed. A hand, sleeve or cable can be caught in the coupling; the guard keeps people and loose items away.

quiz.q: Write the bmep formula and define n<sub>R</sub>.
quiz.a: bmep = 2π n<sub>R</sub> T / V<sub>d</sub>. n<sub>R</sub> is 2 for a four-stroke engine and 1 for a two-stroke engine.

beyond: Not for the exam. Production engine plants use AC transient dynamometers with automated test sequences, and electric vehicle motors are tested on the same beds with regenerative absorption. Research cells add in-cylinder pressure logging and fast emissions benches. Search for 'transient dynamometer driving cycle' and 'AC dynamometer four quadrant'.
